title: feat(plugin-auth): an Okta or Entra ID app tile starts an OIDC sign-in (third-party-initiated login)
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-support-ai"} -->
_Requested by **Yibo Wang** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01BVUyyPie8gHwoPM18iABwB?thread=cmsg_01BVUyyPie8gHwoPM18iABwBDE67gQzDMEEhPfYg79Xcjb)_

Fixes #32086

Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: none

Claim by `domain:server#4` (6764573689); this is item 1, the second of the two PRs seat amendment 6764693228 split the card into (items 2 and 3 landed as #32188). Built under maintainer ruling A on #32150, record 6764924025, and bound by its four points. The entry export of the SAML refusal causes is the seat's order on #32188's review (6769359973, finding c).

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：Okta / Entra ID 应用门户里点 OIDC 应用图标时，IdP 把浏览器带到回调地址，只带 `iss`、不带 code（OIDC Core §4「第三方发起登录」）。以前这一下固定落到 `state_not_found`。现在同一个回调地址上，这种请求在四个条件都满足时，交给 vendor 自己的 `POST /sign-in/sso` 发起标准登录（新的 state 和 PKCE），302 到 IdP。另外按席位要求，从 plugin-auth 入口导出 SAML 拒绝原因列表。
- 为什么改：维护者在 #32150 裁定 A（6764924025）。cloud#3666 在真实 Okta 组织里实测撞上这个错误页，Entra My Apps 同理。
- 风险与回滚：四个条件是 provider 已登记且是 OIDC、`allow_idp_initiated` 开关打开（默认关）、`iss` 与登记的 issuer 逐字节相等、`target_link_uri` 不存在或同源或受信。任一不满足就照旧 `state_not_found`，并写一行 warn。入口不发会话 cookie、不写 `sys_session`，会话只由 vendor 在 IdP 带 code 和匹配的 state 回来、换码和 ID token 验证都通过后创建。不加配置键，回滚即 revert。
- 先看：`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sso-third-party-initiated-login.ts`（门禁和入口），然后 `auth-manager.ts` 里 `runSsoCallback` 末尾的一处挂载。
- 两分钟验证：`cd packages/plugins/plugin-auth && pnpm exec vitest run src/sso-third-party-initiated-login.test.ts`，预期 25 条全过（真实 AuthManager 与 vendor，从 IdP 图标请求走到登录成功，外加四个对照组和七个恶意 `target_link_uri` 对照）。
- 需要你做的：无。这是放宽未登录 GET 能到达的东西，席位按契约复审档复核后落地。

## What changes

**The third-party-initiated entry (item 1).** Okta's OIDC IdP-initiated sign-in in `SPEC` mode, and Entra ID's My Apps, send the browser to the app's initiate login URI carrying `iss` (optionally `target_link_uri`, `login_hint`) and never a `code`. With that URI set to the provider's callback, `@better-auth/sso` 1.7.12 answered `302 …?error=state_not_found`: its `bounceIfIdpInitiated` runs only for a callback with a `code` and no `state`.

- New `sso-third-party-initiated-login.ts`:
  - `thirdPartyInitiatedLoginOf`: the §4 shape is a `GET` with exactly one non-empty `iss` and no `code`, `state` or `error`. Anything else is not the entry's and reaches the vendor untouched.
  - `judgeThirdPartyInitiatedLogin`: the four conditions of ruling 6764924025, first miss wins: `provider_not_registered`, `provider_not_oidc` (a provider without an `oidc_config`; the start also names `providerType: 'oidc'`), `idp_initiated_off` (the #30967 column, read below better-auth like `readSsoProviderSignInOptions` reads it), `issuer_mismatch` (byte-for-byte, no case or trailing-slash folding), `target_link_uri_untrusted` (better-auth's own `isTrustedOrigin`, relative paths allowed, whose list always holds the deployment's origin).
  - `readThirdPartyLoginProvider`: one system-context read of the `sys_sso_provider` row by `provider_id`; no row or a failed read is `provider_not_registered` (fail closed).
  - `runThirdPartyInitiatedLogin`: on a pass, re-dispatches `POST {basePath}/sign-in/sso` `{ providerId, providerType: 'oidc', callbackURL, loginHint? }` through the manager's own `handleRequest`, handed the transport of the callback it serves (#24877). It carries an allow-list of headers, built the way the bridges build theirs: its JSON body type, the request's own `Origin`, and the forwarding facts (`carryForwardedClientAddress`). It never carries a cookie or `authorization`. It answers `302 Location: <the vendor's url>` with the vendor's `Set-Cookie` (the state cookie). `callbackURL` is the checked `target_link_uri`, else `options.baseURL`, where the vendor's own code-without-state bounce lands. A `target_link_uri` sent more than once, or empty, is `target_link_uri_untrusted`, never read as absent. A start the vendor refuses (unverified domain, failed discovery), a non-`http(s)` URL or an unreadable context is `start_refused`. On every miss the vendor callback runs on the request unchanged (today's `state_not_found`) and one `warn` line `{ providerId, entry: 'third_party_initiated', reason }` is written. It carries neither the `iss` nor the target, and it cuts the caller-chosen `providerId` at 128 characters.
- `auth-manager.ts` `runSsoCallback`: an OIDC callback passes the entry first, with the existing refusal scope as its fall-through. `auth-manager-request-routing.ts` hands `runSsoCallback` the transport that `handleRequest` was given, and the entry's re-dispatch passes it on. `sso-oidc-refusal-cause.ts`: the OIDC callback now carries its `request`, as the SAML one does. `sso-sign-in-options.ts`: the stored-boolean rule is exported as `ssoToggleStoredOn` so both readers share it.
- No route-ledger row: the route is the vendor's `/sso/callback/:providerId`, which has none.

**Entry export (seat order).** `index.ts` exports `SSO_SAML_REFUSAL_CAUSES`, `SSO_SAML_UNCLASSIFIED_REFUSAL` and `SsoSamlRefusalCause` beside the OIDC list.

Docs: `content/docs/permissions/sso.mdx` "IdP-initiated sign-in" gains "From an IdP app tile (OIDC third-party-initiated login)" (the URI to set in Okta and Entra ID, the four conditions, the warn reasons, that the request mints nothing), its OIDC "off" bullet names the new shape, and "Why a SAML sign-in was refused" names the exported list.

## Tests

`sso-third-party-initiated-login.test.ts`, END of the chain (a real `AuthManager` and the real `sso()` plugin over the in-memory engine; only the IdP's token and JWKS endpoints are stubbed, the ID token is signed in the test):

- Toggle on and `iss` the registered issuer: `302` to the IdP's authorization endpoint with `client_id`, `redirect_uri` = the callback, a `state`, an S256 `code_challenge` and the `login_hint`; the state cookie is set, **no session cookie, no `sys_session` row**, one `auth-state` verification row, no warn line.
- Finishing it: the IdP's `code` with that `state` and cookie signs the person in through the vendor callback, landing on the base URL; with a trusted `target_link_uri`, landing there.
- **A later callback with a foreign `state` is refused `state_mismatch`; with no `state` the vendor's own bounce restarts at the IdP. Neither signs anyone in.**
- **The four controls of point 3** (toggle off, `iss` off by one character, a SAML provider, an untrusted `target_link_uri`): each answers today's `302 /_console/login?error=state_not_found`, sets no cookie, writes no `auth-state` row and no session, and writes exactly one warn line naming its reason.
- **Hostile `target_link_uri`, against the real vendor matcher.** Each of these answers `state_not_found`, writes no `auth-state` row, and writes one `target_link_uri_untrusted` line:
  - `//host`;
  - `/\host`;
  - userinfo (`http://localhost:3000@attacker.example/…`);
  - a look-alike suffix (`http://localhost:3000.attacker.example/…`);
  - `javascript:`;
  - a repeated target, each value trusted;
  - an empty target.
- **Production posture.** Under `NODE_ENV=production`, with the vendor's origin and callback checks live, the tile start still answers `302` to the IdP. In the same fixture, a cookie-carrying start with no `Origin` is refused `403`, which shows the check is live.
- The warn line carries neither the refused `iss` nor the target; a request with `error` or `state` is the vendor's, untouched.
- Unit:
  - the shape: a duplicate or empty `iss`, `POST`, each excluded parameter, and a repeated or empty `target_link_uri` or `login_hint`;
  - the gate, in order, with byte-for-byte `iss`;
  - the fail-closed row read;
  - the re-dispatch: its body; exactly `content-type`, `origin` (the request's own) and the forwarded headers, with no cookie or `authorization`; only the vendor's URL and state cookie answered;
  - `start_refused`, named for a refused start, a non-`http(s)` URL, a throwing dispatch, a throwing context and a missing base URL;
  - the bounded `providerId`;
  - no read for any other shape.

`bridge-redispatch-transport.pin.test.ts` (#24877): the tile request through the real Hono catch-all is one more row on both branches of the trust rule. With no trusted proxy, its re-dispatched `/sign-in/sso` is judged on the connection peer. Behind a declared `trustProxy`, it is judged on the forwarded client address.

`sso-saml-refusal-cause.test.ts`: the cause list is the one the package entry exports. `sso-saml-refusal-landing.test.ts`: the `ssoCallbackOf` expectation carries the OIDC request.

## Acceptance notes

- Security floor (ruling point 4): an unauthenticated `GET` of the §4 shape on an opted-in provider now gets a `302` to the IdP, a state cookie and one `auth-state` row, where it got `state_not_found`. It reaches nothing `POST /sign-in/sso` does not already give any unauthenticated caller, and only for a provider whose toggle is on. A link on any site can start that flow, as the vendor's own code-without-state bounce already can for the same providers; the person still authenticates at the IdP.
- The re-dispatched start is judged on the same client address as the callback it serves. It is handed the callback's transport, and it carries the forwarding facts, so the vendor's per-address rate limit counts each caller as it counts a direct `POST /sign-in/sso` (review 6772964706, M1).
- `Origin` on the start is the request's own origin, as on the bridges. better-auth 1.7.12 validates `Origin` only on a cookie-carrying request (`origin-check.mjs:108`, `if (!(forceValidate || useCookies)) return;`), and the start carries no cookie. So an ablation that drops the header leaves the production-posture case green. The header is kept for parity with the bridges, and the allow-list unit test pins it.
- Ruling point 1 says an untrusted `target_link_uri` is a miss. That supersedes step 0's "drop it and use the base URL"; the entry refuses instead.
- Delta review 6774305301 left two optional nits, recorded here rather than pushed:
  - `/%2f…` and `/%5c…` targets have no end-of-chain row. better-auth's `isSafeRelativeURL` refuses an encoded path separator (`ENCODED_PATH_SEPARATOR_PATTERN = /%2[fF]|%5[cC]/`, `trusted-origins.mjs`), so either target is a `target_link_uri_untrusted` miss. That comes from reading the source, not from a run.
  - If the vendor refuses the start (its per-address rate limit, an unverified domain, a failed discovery), the person sees today's `state_not_found` and the `warn` line names `start_refused`. The docs name `start_refused` but not the rate-limit case.

## Verification

All runs are at head `7b42be24`, each under `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh`. The head is the round-1 commits `1fdf12d9` and `21140c27` on `main` `02498c9f`, plus the fix commit for contract review 6772964706. CI at `21140c27` was green: 53 check runs, each a success or skipped.

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth exec vitest run`: `Test Files 259 passed (259)`, `Tests 4716 passed | 10 skipped (4726)`, exit 0. The entry's file alone has 25 tests; the transport pin has 20.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth typecheck` (includes `check:test-typecheck`): exit 0.
- Root `eslint` on every touched source and test file: exit 0.
- `node scripts/check-nul-bytes.mjs` and `node scripts/check-commit-card-trailers.mjs --range origin/main..HEAD`: exit 0.
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` derived 105 gates; all 105 ran, each exit 0. `--ran` reports `105 derived, 105 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN`.
- Ablations through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`: 18 of the 19 mutations turned their pin red (child exit 1). `git diff HEAD` was clean after every restore.
  - Round 2:
    - the transport passed into the entry's dispatch, and the transport passed into `runSsoCallback`: the no-proxy branch went red;
    - the forwarded-header carry: the `trustProxy` branch went red;
    - the start's `Origin`: the allow-list unit test went red;
    - an added `authorization` carry: the allow-list unit test went red;
    - the repeated or empty `target_link_uri` miss;
    - `start_refused` for a throwing context;
    - the `providerId` bound;
    - the real matcher swapped for "any non-empty target": five hostile controls went red.
  - The one mutation that stayed green: dropping the start's `Origin` leaves the production-posture case green (child exit 0), as the Acceptance notes explain.
  - Round 1, re-run at this head: the `iss`, toggle, OIDC and target checks; the `state` and `error` exclusions; the passed-on state cookie; the `runSsoCallback` mount; the warn line; landing on the checked target. The deny-list ablation was retired with the deny-list.
- Line budget: 1023 changed lines (+1002 / -21) across 12 files.
